newsitem.title: UK: FT aims to boost US circulation.
newsitem.headline: FT aims to boost US circulation.

text.p: The Financial Times is targeting the US as it aims for "heroic" circulation and profit performances from its Financial Times newspaper, chief executive of the paper's parent Pearson, Marjorie Scardino, said on Monday.
"The US offers us the best potential," Scardino said.
Pearson said it planned to invest up to 100 million pounds over the next five years as part of plans to increase the FT's circulation internationally.
The company said a further 50 million could be spent on promoting the FT and on enhancing production in other Pearson information companies, many of which carry the FT brand.
FT editor Richard Lambert is moving to New York for 12 months from July to oversee editorial developments there.
Andrew Gowers, currently deputy editor, becomes acting editor based in London. Peter Martin will be deputy editor and continue as editor of the international edition.

David Bell, head of Pearson's Information Division, said that north America accounted for only 35,000 out of a total overseas FT daily sale of about 140,000. Total circulation for the newspaper including the UK is around 300,000.
Bell said that the New York edition of the FT was effectively the same as the Frankfurt-printed European edition. "That won't be the case in the future," he said.
Financial daily The Wall Street Journal sells 1.8 million copies in the U.S but Bell said he did not see the FT as a direct competitor.
He said the emphasis in the FT would remain on telling American businessmen what they wanted to know about the world. rather than on domestic issues.
